From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: beth.garcia@atlashealth.com, sre@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly inference surge buffer — proposal & ops asks

Team —

Quick summary: AtlasHealth is running a nightly inference sweep (12:00–03:00 PT) for retrospective scoring. Over the last two weeks their dedicated pool requests have spiked during the 00:30–01:30 window and throttling has caused ~7% job failures. They want a short-term guarantee for a small buffer lane that won't impact other reserved pilots.

I attached a short proposal (nightly_surge_proposal.xlsx) with three options:
- Option A: Dedicated 4-GPU buffer lane (reserved, non-preemptible) for 2 weeks
- Option B: Burst-capacity policy with guaranteed min throughput (soft reservation + preemption fallback)
- Option C: Auto-scale policy tweak (increase max instances during 00:00–03:00 for their pool)

Questions for ops/product:
- What are the risk/impact trade-offs for Option A vs B (latency/SLAs for existing pilots)?
- Can we do a 2-week trial starting next Tuesday, with an automated rollback at end-date?
- Any procurement or billing flags if we treat this as a short-term carve (enterprise pilot with invoice adjustment)?

Action requested: please review the attachment, add comments in the Drive link, and reply with preferred approach + operational blockers by EOD Monday so we can reply to Atlas.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nightly_surge_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet), pool-usage-snapshot-0506.png (image)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: beth.garcia@atlashealth.com, sre@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly inference surge buffer — proposal & ops asks

Hannah — thanks for flagging. High level: Option B is our least disruptive path — it keeps overall fairness while giving them the headroom they need. A few notes from ops perspective:
- We need to ensure the burst lane doesn't force eviction of existing reserved capacity without a policy change; can set a preemption guard (evict low-priority jobs first).
- Monitoring: add a temporary trace for job-level latencies and eviction counts; link back to their account in the Console so CS can see impact in real time.
- Rollback: we can automateset a timeboxed policy with a hard expiry and a webhook to alert the oncall.

Blockers:
1) If Atlas requires non-preemptible reserved nodes (Option A), we'd need sign-off from capacity leads — the pool is near 92% utilization overnight.
2) Billing: short-term dedicated carve requires finance approval for pro-rated credits if we make capacity commitments.

I'll put an ops runbook stub into the Drive folder. If Atlas is OK with soft reservations, we can do Option B as a 2-week test starting Tue 2027-05-11.

-Kimberly
Director, Infra Ops

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly inference surge buffer — proposal & ops asks

Folks — a few capacity-scheduling notes from product infra:
- If we open a hard 4-GPU buffer (Option A) we need to rebalance across pools. That will increase average token latency for a subset of low-priority pilots unless we shift some soft-scheduled work to daytime windows. Not ideal during heavy sprint periods.
- Option C (auto-scale tweaks) is attractive if their job patterns are predictable — we can tune max instances and cooldown windows to reduce churn. But it requires a short model of cost delta; I estimate +12% token cost during the 3 hour window for their model profile.

Recommendation: start with Option B (burst policy) + telemetry. If burst shows >90% eviction on other pilots, pivot to Option C or negotiate a paid short-term carve (Option A).

I'll sync with Aditya on billing impacts and get a cost delta spreadsheet Monday.

-Marcus
Principal Product Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly inference surge buffer — proposal & ops asks

Quick billing note: if we treat this as a short-term dedicated carve and issue a credit for impacted tenants, Finance will want a one-pager describing the business rationale and the exact invoice adjustments. For Option B (burst), there's minimal billing change — we bill actual consumption. Option A needs manual pro-rating or a short-term amendment.

I've started Draft:INF-1426 in Jira with the proposed billing paths and a sample amendment clause; Laura, can you review the wording for legal/contract touchpoints?

-Aditya
Senior Revenue Operations Manager

Thanks everyone — copying next steps and a reply to Atlas below.

Reply to Atlas (draft):
Hi Beth / Atlas SRE team — thanks for the heads up and the usage snapshot. We can support a short 2-week trial with a burst-capacity policy (Option B) starting Tue, 2027-05-11.
- What we'll do: enable a soft-reservation burst lane during 00:00–03:00 PT for your pool, instrument additional telemetry, and set an automatic rollback on 2027-05-25.
- If we observe >90% eviction impact on other reserved pilots, we'll reach back to discuss either (a) migrating the sweep window or (b) a paid short-term dedicated carve (4 GPUs) for the remainder of the trial.
- Action for Atlas: confirm the sweep start time (preferred window?) and share the job-ids/labels so we can attach tracing.

Internal next steps:
1) Kimberly: implement burst policy + runbook + console trace (deadline Tue morning)
2) Marcus: cost delta spreadsheet & eviction thresholds (Mon end)
3) Aditya: draft amendment language in Jira (INF-1426) and notify Finance/Legal
4) Hannah: send final confirmation to Atlas once internal OK

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
